parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer with a comparatively protective division. Universal federal exposure dominates: binary sex on visas/passports, instructed refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, a possible fraud-based lifetime bar, exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities, and documented severe abuse in federal/immigration custody. The division adds none of these for adults — it has gender-identity public-accommodation and hate-crime protections, easy state documents, and a July 2026 low-risk assessment. Division exposures concentrate on minors (school facility/pronoun bans, athletics bar, provider ban on changing a minor's identity). Remedies are real but contested and unresolved. Net: entry friction and exclusion with humiliation, occasional detention carrying documented custody harm, but no criminalisation of adult presence in the division.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility considered; X markers barred; foreign governments issued travel advisories for trans citizens. Documented, universal for outed visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; civil-liberties suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Division-issued ID with X or changed marker can conflict with federal binary screening, triggering discrepancy review and refusal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cut, hormones removed); immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse against trans detainees. State-instigated, severe if detained.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Division hate-crime statute and panic-defence repeal; national courts have enjoined several orders; several orders blocked.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border document discrepancy can escalate into federal custody, where birth-sex placement and care denial apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars federally funded single-sex facilities by birth sex. Division: 2023 education-department bathroom/pronoun ban (reversal intended, status uncertain), athletics bar; no general adult facility ban documented in the division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division public-accommodation law covers gender identity; 2014 ruling protecting student bathroom use stands; map shows 29 units without bans.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule applies even where division public-accommodation law protects, since federal funding conditions bind institutions.

care_services.exposure: Division prohibits providers changing a minor's gender identity — a visiting minor risks refused HRT/care. Federal funding freezes and proposed under-18 insurance bar.
care_services.protection: No adult care restriction documented in the division; adult emergency care not shown restricted.
care_services.interaction: A family's care-seeking can trigger provider refusal and, under federal school orders, official scrutiny of the child's transition.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups, DOJ reward memo, dehumanising executive-order language, 66% public support for birth-sex documents; advocates compare trajectory to genocide's early stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division hate-crime law, civil-rights statute, low-risk July 2026 assessment for adults; hostile rhetoric not documented as operational against visitors here.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National framing raises discretionary hostility at federal desks while division institutions remain protective.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division school facility/pronoun bans, athletics association bar, provider ban on changing minors' identity; federal order directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition and investigation of schools.
minors_guardians.protection: 2014 ruling allowing student bathroom use stands; policies intended for reversal in 2026; assessment says youth policies unlikely to extend to adults (not to minors).
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting guardian accompanying a trans minor in any school-linked setting encounters both division school rules and federal investigation risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific figures on hate-crime enforcement or violence against transgender people appear in the sources; national bias statistics cover sexual orientation only. Absence is not safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime statute expressly covers gender identity (2020); gay/trans panic defence repealed 2021.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists on paper; actual enforcement frequency for trans visitors is unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and health rules unresolved; whether 2023 school policies were reversed unestablished; equality-map URL 404; fraud-finding waiver limited; no division violence data.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation with several orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ; functioning division courts and civil-rights enforcement; public-accommodation complaints route.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A traveller's real-time exposure shifts with which federal measure is in force on the travel date.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far above this anchor: no morality sweeps, no arrest for public presentation, no coercive prosecution or credible capital clause in the division, and remedies (courts, civil-rights statute) demonstrably function. Federal custody abuse exists but only on detention, not as routine street policing.

Somewhat above: entry refusal and facility exclusion are instructed and near-universal for outed visitors, but there is no visitor conduct register, no airline-imposed exclusion, the division affirmatively protects public accommodations, and litigation offers a real (if uncertain) remedy that appeals there almost never grant.

Closest analogue: extended secondary screening, discretionary refusal of entry, administrative rather than criminal outcomes, slow and rarely revised remedies. This dossier matches that tier, adding a documented custody-harm pathway and stronger division protections — netting to roughly the same level.

Materially below: here markers cannot match presentation, officers are instructed to refuse discrepant cases, exclusion from federally funded facilities is state policy, and custody carries documented abuse. There is no trained-inspection regime, no recognition of congruent markers, and no compensation-for-detention pathway.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences one system, not two: federal entry screening, federal facility rules and federal custody bind regardless of the division's equality statutes. The federal layer supplies the heaviest exposures — instructed refusal on document discrepancy, possible lifetime fraud bar, facility exclusion, and severe documented custody abuse — none of which division protections can pre-empt. The division supplies the mitigations: public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage reaching visitors, accessible state documents as a climate signal, functioning courts, and a low-risk assessment for adults. Division restrictions concentrate on minors, so an adult alone fares better than a family with a trans child. Unresolved litigation and missing violence data keep the rating mid-scale rather than in the reduced-risk band.
